newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada set to raise Clyde offer-paper.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada set to raise Clyde offer-paper.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd is expected to increase its offer for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc to 120 pence ($1.92) per share from 105 pence, the Daily Telegraph reported on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the increase would upset investors, who had been expecting substantially more.

Gulf Canada launched its 432 million pound ($692.6 million) offer for the UK oil exploration and production firm on December 18. An offer of 120 pence per share would value Clyde at 494 million pounds ($792 million).
Clyde's shares added 2-1/2 pence to close at 118 pence on the London stock exchange on Monday.

The shares have consistently been trading well above Gulf Canada's bid price amid market hopes of a counter bid. Several industry analysts have said they did not expect Clyde to be taken out for less than 125 pence per share.
But the Daily Telegraph cited broker NatWest Securities as saying that an increased offer of 120 pence may be "just enough to win the day". ($1=.6237 Pound)
